The Nodal Court

One court, eight phones. This diagram is drawn to true proportions — 23.77 m long × 10.97 m wide (doubles) — with the 8 recommended nodal points: 2 centred HIGH behind each baseline, 4 LOW–MID on the corner diagonals, and 2 MID at the net posts. Tap any point to see its job and give it a holder.

Point waiting for a holder Holder assigned Dashed ring = the point's view of the court
Coverage rule: a point of play only counts if at least 4 line intersections are seen across the node views. Every point below is placed to see 5–9 intersections on its own — the geometry does the work before any software does.

Tap a point on the court

Each of the 8 points has a different job. Pick one to read its role and assign who is holding that phone. Use pseudonyms — no real names needed.

3

Calibration Ritual

How a pinned court earns its badge: five steps, under five minutes, clock running. Finish everything before the timer hits zero and the badge is decided by the real rules — VERIFIED needs at least 3 distinct holders across at least 2 court ends with every step passed. Anything less is PROVISIONAL, with the reason shown. No shortcuts, no honorary badges.

5:00
hard fail at zero

Not started. Assign holders in Section 2 first if you want Step 2 to pass — the ritual reads the same crew.

Node readings in this walkthrough are simulated node readings — on a real court these come from the phones at the 8 nodal points. The steps, tolerances and badge rules are the real design.
Step 1 · Pin & template

Confirm the court, prove one real distance

Confirm the court's template matches the ground, then measure one real distance — baseline to baseline is the honest one (true: 23.77 m). Your measurement must land within 2%.

Step 2 · Place & register

Every point placed, every holder recorded

All 8 nodal points must be placed, each seeing ≥ 4 line intersections, and each with a holder recorded in Section 2. This step reads your crew live.

Step 3 · Walk the corners

Four corners, one court — agree within ±15 cm

Walk to each corner. The nodes triangulate each corner's position; the four readings must agree within ±15 cm or the template is lying.

No readings yet.

Step 4 · Five-spot bounce test

Call five bounces — two of them straddle a line

The app drops 5 test bounces on the court. Tap a spot, then call it IN or OUT (a ball touching the line is IN). The nodes' simulated readings must get both straddles right and at least 4 of 5 overall — and so must you.

Tap a numbered spot to select it.

Your calls: 0 / 5 · Node readings (simulated): waiting

Step 5 · Sync & 30-second drill

Frames in step, then prove it live

All phones must sync frames within ~33 ms (one frame at 30 fps), then hold together through a 30-second rally drill. In this demo the drill runs at 10× speed — 3 seconds.

Replay Call

Keep score, and when a bounce is disputed, call it with the nodes. Three camera angles report where the ball landed; the house verifier (v0.2) turns their readings into a verdict — counting distinct holders, never devices, and demanding the agreeing readings cluster within ±15 cm.
